thread:
jamie (support): FYI escalation from Acme — they rotated their API key ~2h ago via the dashboard but are still seeing successful 200s and billing for requests using the OLD key. customer says rotation reported 'disabled' in vault UI. Can auth team take a look?

acme-support: We rotated from key_abc123 -> key_def456 at 2026-03-17T10:12:00Z. We believe rotation completed, but our mobile clients still get successful responses when using key_abc123. We can provide request ids.

jamie (support): Example request id: rq_20260317_001 (we have full headers/logs). Quick repro curl they ran:

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer key_abc123" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

priya (auth): Thanks. Quick questions: when you say 'disabled in vault UI', do you mean vault kv entry set to disabled or the API Key service marked disabled? (different code paths). Also, did you use the 'Rotate key' flow in the console or a manual create/delete?

acme-support: We used the console rotate button. It showed success, new key present and old key marked disabled. We did not delete the old key.

michael (edge): Pinging because this smells like an edge-side cache TTL. We have a token introspection cache at the CDN/edge that caches positive validation results for 5m by default (config edge.auth.cache_ttl). But 2 hours is much longer. Did you happen to hit a proxied CDN with sticky caching? Any chance a downstream proxy or mobile CDN cached Authorization header?

acme-support: We're using our own CDN in front of you (FastEdge) for client traffic to reduce latency. Could FastEdge be caching 200 responses regardless of auth header? We configured cache-by-header but might be misconfigured.

jamie (support): I pulled token validation logs from our auth-service for rq_20260317_001 — auth-service shows a revocation event for key_abc123 at 2026-03-17T10:12:07Z and subsequent introspection calls returning 401 for that key from our origin. But the gateway logs show a 200 served from edge cache at 10:14:02Z. So timeline: revocation -> auth shows 401 -> edge still served cached 200.

priya (auth): That matches. Our introspection publishes invalidation events to the cache layer via /cache-invalidate endpoint, but the edge layer has an additional HTTP-level CDN in front (customer-controlled) that can serve cached responses if it ignores Authorization variations. Michael, can edge infra confirm whether our cache-invalidation webhook reached the CDN?

michael (edge): Looking at our side, we sent cache-invalidate for key_abc123 at 10:12:08Z with 200. But we also saw ~18ms spike errors to the external CDN endpoint (acme's FastEdge) around that time — connection resets. If their CDN didn't accept the purge, it would keep serving stale cached objects keyed by URL only. Unfortunately some customers configure their CDN to ignore Authorization when computing cache key.

acme-support: Confirmed: FastEdge had a misconfig where "cache_key": ["path", "query"] only. Auth header not part of key. They also set a long TTL for /v1/generate responses (max-age=7200).

jamie (support): Okay — root cause appears to be a customer CDN configuration that caches authenticated endpoints and ignored the Authorization header, combined with missed purge due to a transient network error during our purge call. Workarounds: 1) purge FastEdge cache manually (they can do this), 2) change origin to send Cache-Control: no-store for endpoints requiring active auth (we can push a quick header tweak), 3) expire keys and issue new ones and rotate client config to use only new key (nuclear).

priya (auth): Short-term action we can take: mark key_abc123 as force-expired at the gateway layer (edge will check local revocation cache before serving cached 200 if we enable 'auth-bypass-protect' flag). I can flip that flag for the tenant. That will cause the edge to drop cached responses that were served with that auth token (best effort). Need approval from oncall.

sre-oncall: Approving. Flip it and log a note. Also add a transient metric to watch for repeat stale-200s.

michael (edge): Done. Flipped auth-bypass-protect for tenant acme-inc at 10:20:30Z. Pushed header override: Cache-Control: no-cache for subsequent origin responses. Also resent cache-purge to FastEdge at 10:20:35Z — got 202 accepted.

acme-support: After your action we see requests with old key now getting 401. Thanks. Can you also add a short doc to explain recommended CDN config (include Authorization in cache key) and a pre-rotation checklist for customers that have external CDNs? We got burned because the dashboard rotate flow didn't warn about external caching.

jamie (support): Copying action items: 1) Priya to add temporary flag docs and long-term plan to detect CDNs that ignore auth. 2) Michael to add dashboard warning for "external CDN configured" if we detect cached edge after rotation (heuristic). 3) Support to update customer-facing rotation checklist and include command to purge upstream CDN.

priya (auth): I'll open a short ticket to change default Cache-Control for authenticated endpoints to no-store and to surface stronger heuristics when rotation happens. Ticket: AUTH-7462.

michael (edge): I'll add a heartbeat to our purge webhook retry logic to be more aggressive on failures (EDGE-1298). Also adding a dashboard event when revocation doesn't immediately reduce successful token counts in top-20 gateways.

jamie (support): Customer follow-up: Acme will run a full rotate+purge test with us tomorrow. They've asked for a contact for assisted purge if their CDN fails. We'll provide SRE contact.

acme-support: Thanks all, appreciate quick response and workaround. :thumbsup:
